claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain James F. Ranney is the Akron radio engineer, Signal Corps officer, and OSS Area C communications instructor documented by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and middle initial, commissioned-grade sequence, Signal Corps schooling, Area C instruction, and later overseas communications work align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact name plus several specific military and OSS identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences civilian radio engineering, the draft and Signal Corps officer training, spring 1943 OSS recruitment, and Area C service beginning in August 1943.
claims.match_notes: Box 632 remains unreviewed. The index's Captain grade is compatible with promotion after the official account's spring 1943 second-lieutenant commission.

claims.claim_text: Ranney's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the United States Army Signal Corps.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says he was drafted, attended Signal Corps Officer Candidate School, and was recruited by OSS upon graduating as a second lieutenant in spring 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, commissioned-grade, and Area C instructor match.
claims.match_notes: Signal Corps service is not classified as civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: Before he was drafted, Ranney worked as an engineer at an unnamed radio station in Youngstown, Ohio.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history supplies the occupation and city but does not identify the station.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, Signal Corps, and OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented before the draft; the exact employment dates and final day before service are not stated.
claims.match_notes: No reliable named pre-OSS radio-station employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Spyridon G. Kapponnis is Spyridon George Kapponnis, also known as Spiro Cappony, the USNR radio operator recruited into OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS supplies the full middle name and alias; a contemporaneous OSS mission report independently names Spyridon G. Kapponnis as a USNR radio operator.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare exact name and middle initial, full-name expansion, alias, USNR status, radio specialty, and OSS mission context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences Michigan State College attendance, 1943 Navy entry and radio school, OSS recruitment, and the 1944 Evros mission.
claims.match_notes: Box 390 remains unreviewed; the blank index rank is preserved while the direct mission report supplies the wartime USNR grade and role.

claims.claim_text: Kapponnis's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was United States Navy service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS explicitly says the Communications Branch recruited him from the Navy after boot camp and naval radio communications school.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the rare-name, USNR, radio-operator, and Greece mission match.
claims.match_notes: The contemporaneous mission report corroborates USNR status but is not used to establish the earlier transfer date.

claims.claim_text: Before joining the Navy, Kapponnis attended Michigan State College.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says he left the college in 1943 at age 20 to join the Navy.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same rare-name official biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student affiliation followed by Navy service before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Michigan State College is not presented as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed T-5 Arthur F. Reinhardt is the Army Air Corps communications trainee and OSS radio operator described by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and middle initial, enlisted technical grade, radio specialty, Area C training, and China service align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact name plus compatible technical grade and unusually specific OSS communications chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history places high-school graduation and Army Air Corps entry in 1943, OSS recruitment after communications school, and Area C training beginning in June 1944.
claims.match_notes: Box 638 remains unreviewed. The index note 'extract fr' is preserved as printed and not expanded without archival evidence.

claims.claim_text: Reinhardt's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the United States Army Air Corps.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says he joined the Air Corps, attended its communications school at Scott Field, and was recruited by OSS after placing near the top of the class.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, enlisted technical-grade, and radio-operator match.
claims.match_notes: The family farm is not inferred to be Reinhardt's employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed T-4 Gail F. Donnalley is the Ohio Wesleyan student and OSS cryptologist documented by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and middle initial, compatible technical-sergeant grade, Ohio background, Area C training, and cryptology assignment align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact name plus compatible grade and specific official OSS training and assignment details.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history says OSS recruited Donnalley during his sophomore year and places his Area C training in October 1943.
claims.match_notes: Box 193 remains unreviewed. The printed T-4 rank is preserved; the official history's later Technical Sergeant reference is compatible with advancement.

claims.claim_text: Donnalley's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was student status at Ohio Wesleyan University.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says he was recruited by OSS during his sophomore year at Ohio Wesleyan.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, compatible-grade, and cryptology match.
claims.match_notes: Ohio Wesleyan is not classified as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed John W. Brunner is the Philadelphia classical-languages student, Army language trainee, and OSS cryptologist documented by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and middle initial, Philadelphia origin, 1943 draft, Army Chinese-language course, and OSS cryptology assignment align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact name plus several specific military, educational, geographic, and OSS identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences college study, the 1943 draft, Army-directed Chinese study, OSS recruitment less than a year later, and Area C training in October 1944.
claims.match_notes: Box 89 remains unreviewed; the private service number strengthens future archival resolution but is not displayed in full publicly.

claims.claim_text: Brunner's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was United States Army service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says the Army sent Brunner to study Chinese and that OSS recruited him with another top student less than a year later.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, Philadelphia, Army-language-course, and cryptology match.
claims.match_notes: The Berkeley course is treated as an Army assignment, not civilian university employment.

claims.claim_text: Before he was drafted, Brunner studied classical Greek and Latin at a college that the accessible source does not identify.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history documents the subjects and student status but names no institution.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name and documented Army-to-OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student affiliation ending with his 1943 draft.
claims.match_notes: No college has been guessed or assigned from unrelated namesake results.

research_attempts.query_text: "James F Ranney" OSS; Signal Corps; Youngstown radio station engineer; employer; NARA index and web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, broadcasting, newspaper, obituary, directory, institutional, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Search snippets, an unrelated railroad result, postwar amateur-radio references, and records lacking the Signal Corps and OSS chronology were not used as employer evidence; no accessible source reliably named the Youngstown station.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the explicit Signal Corps predecessor and published only the unnamed civilian occupation, without inventing a station.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 632 and Youngstown broadcasting directories.

research_attempts.query_text: "Spyridon G Kapponnis" OSS; "Spyridon George Kapponnis"; "Spiro Cappony"; USNR radio operator; Michigan State College; NARA index and web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, direct Evros Mission report, institutional, obituary, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Genealogy and namesake results, search snippets, and derivative summaries were rejected as final evidence; the CIA discovery result was not retained because its direct URL redirected in this environment, while a visually reviewed direct OSS mission scan supplied the same identity corroboration.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the student-to-Navy-to-OSS sequence and independently corroborated the exact USNR radio-operator identity in a direct 1944 mission report.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 390 for Navy transfer paperwork and any earlier civilian employer.

research_attempts.query_text: "Arthur F Reinhardt" OSS; T-5; Army Air Corps; Scott Field communications; employer; NARA index and web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, military, newspaper, obituary, institutional, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: An unrelated 1965 directory entry, common-name results, derivative summaries, and records lacking the T-5, Air Corps, or OSS context were rejected; the family farm was not assumed to be employment.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the explicit Air Corps predecessor and preserved the absence of a reliable civilian-employer finding.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 638 and pre-1943 family-farm records.

research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 193 and wartime Ohio Wesleyan records.
